title: A Toolkit to Enable Hydrocarbon Conversion in Aqueous Environments
protocol: Digest the donor BioBrick with EcoRI and SpeI for positioning the donor part downstream of the acceptor part.
Digest the donor BioBrick with XbaI and PstI for positioning the donor part upstream of the acceptor part.
Add an appropriate restriction enzyme that cuts in the backbone of the donor to digest up to 1.0 μg of DNA.
Digest the acceptor BioBrick with EcoRI and XbaI or SpeI and PstI.
Incubate all digestions for at least one hour at 37°C.
Inactivate the restriction endonucleases by heat incubation at 80°C for 10 min followed by centrifugation.
Ligate the digested BioBrick parts (donor and acceptor) together with T4 ligation buffer and T4 ligase in a total volume of 10-15 μl.
Incubate the ligation mixture at 16°C for at least three hours.
Perform transformation reaction with approximately half of the ligation mix.
Confirm the BioBrick sequence is correct through sequencing.
Use JCat website tool to modify genes for optimal expression in E. coli from synthesized DNA.
Make further modifications according to the BioBrick standard requirements.
Culture E. coli cells expressing the Alkane Hydroxylase system (BBa_K398014) in 5 ml LB medium with appropriate antibiotics overnight.
Culture E. coli cells carrying an empty vector (BBa_J13002) in 5 ml LB medium with appropriate antibiotics overnight.
Transfer 500 μl of overnight culture into 50 ml of fresh LB with antibiotic.
Incubate until cell turbidity reaches an OD600 of 0.3.
Centrifuge for 10 min at 4,000 rpm.
Resuspend the pellet in 5 ml of 0.1 M phosphate buffer (pH 7.4).
Centrifuge again for 10 min at 4,000 rpm.
Resuspend the pellet in 5 ml of 0.1 M phosphate buffer containing E2 salts and 0.66% v/v glycerol.
Measure cell turbidity (OD600).
Prepare cell-mixture aliquots of 6 ml in 25 ml closed-cap glass flasks.
Add no-cell controls with E2 salts and 0.66% v/v glycerol.
Add 100 nmol of alkane to each flask.
Incubate mixtures at 37 °C for 24 hr (shorten if higher rates are obtained).
Measure OD600 after incubation.
Extract hydrocarbons in culture media by ethyl acetate.
Determine hydrocarbon concentration in cell culture by gas chromatography.
Calculate degradation per unit of biomass by dividing the total amount of alkane converted by the total biomass present in each flask (convert OD600 to dry weight).
Divide the result by experimental duration to yield degradation activity per unit biomass per time unit.
Take the average from three individual runs.
Culture E. coli cells expressing the ladA gene in 50 ml LB medium with appropriate antibiotics overnight.
Transfer 500 μl of the overnight culture into 50 ml of fresh LB (with antibiotic) and incubate until the cell turbidity reaches an optical density of 0.6 at 600 nm.
Centrifuge the cells for 10 min at 4,000 rpm at 4 °C and resuspend the pellet in 5 ml of 50 mM Tris buffer.
Sonicate the cells at 40% duty cycle with an output control of 4 while keeping the solution on ice.
Centrifuge the resulting mixture for 5 min at 4,000 rpm at 4 °C to remove cell debris.
Transfer the supernatant to a fresh vial.
Determine the total protein concentration of the cell extracts by Bradford assay.
Prepare a 100 ml mixture containing 0.1% v/v alkane and 50 mM Tris-HCl buffer.
Heat the mixture at 100 °C for 5 min.
Sonicate the warm mixture for 1 min until a homogeneous, viscous solution is obtained.
Add 1 mM of NADH, 1 mM FMN, 1 mM MgSO4 and 0.01 v/v Triton X-100 to the solution.
Prepare 6 ml aliquots in 25 ml closed-cap flasks.
Add adequate amounts of cell extract based on Bradford assays (final concentration of 5 mg protein/l).
Prepare a no-protein control.
Incubate at 60 °C for 24 hr.
Extract hydrocarbons in the culture media by ethyl acetate.
Determine hydrocarbon concentration in cell culture by gas chromatography.
Calculate degradation per unit of biomass by dividing total amount of alkane converted by total protein added to each flask (by Bradford calibration curve).
Further divide by experiment duration to yield degradation activity per unit of cellular protein per time unit.
Take the average from three individual runs.
Add 2.5 ml ethyl acetate to 6 ml experimental solution.
Add an internal standard to the solvent at a concentration of 0.1 % (v/v).
Optionally, add Triton X-100 to the aqueous mixture and centrifuge samples for 10 min at 4,000 rpm.
Vortex the mixture for 5 sec (1,500 rpm).
Incubate the mixture at room temperature until the two phases separate.
Remove a maximal amount of the organic layer and dry the solvent using anhydrous magnesium sulphate.
Filter the mixture through 0.2 μm filter to remove MgSO4.
Transfer filtrate into gas chromatograph vials for measurements or store at -20°C.
Determine concentration by gas chromatography using CP-SIL 5CB column (length = 5 m).
Inject 10 μl of sample in split mode (1:10, 230 °C) with helium flow rate of 1 ml/min.
Perform oven temperature program starting at 50°C for 7.5 min, then increase to 90°C at a rate of 50°C per minute and continue the programmed steps as specified.
Integrate peaks and correct concentrations with respect to the internal standard.
Culture E. coli cells expressing ADH or ALDH gene in 50 ml LB medium overnight.
Transfer 500 μl of overnight culture into fresh 50 ml LB and incubate until OD600 reaches 0.6.
Centrifuge for 10 min at 4,000 rpm at 4°C.
Resuspend the pellet in 5 ml of 50 mM Tris buffer.
Sonicate the cell solution at 40% duty cycle with an output control of 4, keeping the solution on ice during sonication.
Centrifuge the resulting mixture for 5 min at 4,000 rpm at 4°C to remove cell debris.
Determine the total protein concentration of the cell extracts by Bradford assay using a glass vial.
Load a 96 well plate with 180 μl 57 mM glycine buffer containing NAD (final concentration 1 mM, pH 9.5) in each well.
Add 5 μl of the alcohol (aldehyde) to be tested to the wells.
Heat long chain alcohols before starting the assay to ensure they are liquid.
For each alcohol (aldehyde), add a control without substrate as a negative control.
Prepare a blank containing a mixture of buffer and the substrate without cell extract.
Preheat the plate reader for 15 min at 37°C to allow equilibration of the system.
Add adequate amounts of cell extract based on Bradford assays, with a final concentration of 5 mg protein/l.
Prepare a no-protein control.
Measure NADH production using a spectrophotometer at a wavelength of 340 nm every 2-3 min for 1 hr at 37°C.
Calculate the NADH production rate from the slope of the OD measurement at 340 nm.
Take into account the light path length and the extinction coefficient of NADH (6220 M-1cm-1).
Divide the NADH production rate by the total amount of protein added to express the activity of the dehydrogenase reaction in the cell extract (U/mg whole cell protein).
Calculate the mean and the standard deviation from three independent runs.
Culture E. coli cells expressing the pCaiF-GFP construct overnight in 5 ml LB medium with appropriate antibiotics.
Inoculate 5 ml M9 containing 10 g/l glucose and antibiotics with 50 μl of the overnight culture and grow overnight.
Subculture 50 μl of the overnight outgrowth into 5 ml of fresh M9 with 10 g/l and incubate until the cell turbidity reaches an optical density of 0.2 at 600 nm.
Load a 96 well plate with 100 μl of fresh M9 medium containing the desired amount of carbon source for testing in each well.
Perform triplicate experiments for statistical evaluation and add the respective negative controls (wild-type E. coli K12).
Add 5 μl of the overnight culture to the medium-containing wells.
Measure the growth curve (OD600) and GFP fluorescence (485 nm excitation and 520 emission) using a plate reader every 10 min for 18 hr at 37 °C with constant shaking.
Calculate the growth rate from the measurements.
Calculate the specific GFP content from the measurements.
Compare the calculated values to the control.
Calculate the mean of at least three independent experiments.
Calculate the standard deviation of at least three independent experiments.
Culture E. coli expressing PhPFDα and β gene overnight in 5 ml LB medium with appropriate antibiotics.
Subculture 10 μl of the overnight culture into fresh 5 ml LB (with antibiotic).
Incubate until cell turbidity reaches an OD600 of 0.3 to 0.4.
Dilute the cultures with fresh medium until an OD600 of 0.1 is reached.
Load a 96 well plate with 180 μl M9 medium containing appropriate antibiotics and toxic compound in triplicate.
Add 20 μl of the culture (control) into the wells.
Measure the biomass concentration (OD600) using a plate reader every 10 min for 24 hours at 37 °C with constant shaking.
Calculate the growth rates from the respective measurements for different agent concentrations and compare to the negative control.
Calculate the mean and the standard deviation of at least three independent runs.
